items.title: Watching America Run Away With AI - Alistair Pullen (Cosine AI)
items.summary:
This episode is sponsored by Notion. Learn more about Notion's Developer Platform today at https://notion.com/mlst

Britain's most capable coding model can't be exported, and that ban is the whole reason Cosine set out to build one from scratch. Alistair Pullen, CEO and co-founder of Cosine, sits down with Tim Scarfe to explain how a frontier system he calls Fable, locked behind US export controls, became the founding case for a UK sovereign model trained on the Isambard supercomputer in Bristol.

The bet underneath it is economic. Pullen argues that an inference company, rather than a training-first lab, doesn't need billions to compete: millions, a national compute allocation, and a consortium feedback loop can be enough. From there it gets into the machinery, why open-weight models still trail the frontier on size, active parameters and data, the mixture-of-experts versus dense trade-off and why active params dominate how a model actually feels, and the edge that real coding trajectories confer.

The back half is about making agents trustworthy. Pullen makes the case for beating "slop" by rewarding the process instead of the final answer, reframes code review as runtime proof (spin the bug up in a VM and force the agent to actually exploit it), and walks through Swarm, Cosine's system running hundreds of sub-agents in one shot. It ends on why memory is still an unsolved hack, how synthetic graders let you run RL on tasks with no built-in test, and why Pullen reads US export controls as an accidental gift, with a supply-chain sting in the tail.

items.title: The Tipping Point That Caused 80X AI Growth
items.summary: In episode 1007 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Benjamin Todd, President of 80000 Hours about how AI workers could revolutionize business coordination. Todd explains how AI systems can communicate instantly across firms and receive direct CEO supervision, eliminating the communication overhead that slows human organizations. This coordination advantage could allow AI companies to move dramatically faster than traditional businesses.

items.title: Build A Custom Browser Extension [SUPER Easy!]
items.summary:
I built a fully functioning Chrome extension in about 10 minutes.

I used the new GLM 5.2 model to build it. It's open-weight, open-source and incredibly cost-effective for coding tasks while still being reliable and delivery high-quality outputs (not sponsored, just sharing because I like it a lot). 

Once you run the prompt, here's how you install it:
1️⃣ Save the files generated by GLM 5.2 (or whichever AI model you choose for this) into a folder on your computer.
2️⃣ Open Google Chrome, click the three dots in the top right, and go to Extensions ➡️ Manage Extensions (or type chrome://extensions/ in your search bar).
3️⃣ Toggle on Developer Mode in the top right-hand corner.
4️⃣ Click Load unpacked in the top left, and select your folder.

Just like that, your custom extension is installed and ready to use.

📌 SAVE this video so you can refer back to the steps later, and follow for more practical AI tips!

#AI #AITools #AICoding #OpenSourceAI #TechTips

items.title: When a Feature Request is Vague or Urgent, How Do You Decide the Right Architecture?
items.summary:
When the request is vague, urgent, and “just needs to ship,” it’s tempting to add code now and worry about scale later.

But that’s exactly how small decisions turn into expensive architecture problems.

In this short, Matt Erman, author of Grokking Software Architecture, explains how to make smarter architecture choices when the future is unclear: how to think about tradeoffs, avoid overengineering, and still leave your system room to grow.

If you’ve ever heard “we’ll fix it later” and felt your soul leave your body, this one’s for you.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04gYZN10

items.title: RAG Has Evolved into Multi-modal AI Search Agents (RL, HaPO)
items.summary:
Years ago we started with RAG and Vector Embeddings, then we moved to Agentic RAG systems and today we discover multi-modal AI Search Agents, which we train with SFT and RL (HaPO, a GRPO based optimization with step-level rewards) for optimal search results. 

RAG has a huge evolution trace. And today we look at SearchEyes.

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Game Theory
items.summary:
Discover how game theory can improve real-world decision-making—no interest in games or background in game theory required! This concise, practical introduction led by Wolfram game theory kernel developer Marc Vicuna introduces built-in game theory functions in Wolfram Language. Learn to work with matrix games, the Nash equilibrium, tree games, repeated games and evolutionary equilibria.

Every lesson has interactive visualizations that make player choices and outcomes easy to understand, along connections from the "game" to other contexts such as business, economics and other everyday strategizing.

Ready to dive in? Enroll in the full course at https://wolfr.am/Intro-Game-Theory to get video lessons, practice exercises, instant feedback quizzes, a scratch notebook for your own code and access to an AI course assistant to help when you need it.

#WolframU #GameTheory #WolframLanguage
